column5: THE STEEL CIRCLE: A Samurai Chronology From the birth of the Shogun to the death of the sword. This list tracks the evolution of the warrior class through nearly 1,000 years of Japanese history. I. THE ANCIENT ROOTS Before the samurai were rulers, they were the elite blade for the Imperial Court. Rashomon (1950) | Setting: c. 700s–1100s (Heian Period) | Civil decay and the instability of truth in an ancient, crumbling world. The Men Who Tread on the Tiger's Tail (1945) | Setting: 1185 (Genpei War) | The legendary conflict that birthed the very first Shogunate and established the warrior class. II. THE AGE OF CHAOS The "Warring States" era where the land was soaked in blood and the gods were fading. Onibaba (1964) | Setting: 1330s (Nanboku-chō Period) | A harrowing look at survival and horror for the common folk during the War of Two Courts. Princess Mononoke (1997) | Setting: c. 1450 (Muromachi Period) | The transition from a mystical age of spirits to an industrial age defined by iron and gunpowder. Throne of Blood (1957) | Setting: 15th Century (Early Sengoku) | A Shakespearean descent into madness and ambition in a lawless, fog-shrouded land. Ran (1985) | Setting: 16th Century (Mid-Sengoku) | A grand, color-coded epic depicting the tragic decline of a powerful warlord and his divided house. Seven Samurai (1954) | Setting: 1587 (Late Sengoku) | The peak of civil war. Masterless ronin and desperate peasants find common ground in the mud. Ugetsu (1953) | Setting: Late 1500s | An ethereal, ghostly masterpiece showing the supernatural and tragic cost of war on the civilian family. III. THE TOKUGAWA ASCENT Unification, isolation, and the establishment of a 250-year peace. Shōgun (2024) | Setting: 1600 (Battle of Sekigahara) | The pivotal chess match for the soul of Japan and the rise of the Tokugawa dynasty. The Samurai Trilogy (1954–1956) | Setting: 1600–1612 | Following Musashi Miyamoto as he transitions from a raw soldier at Sekigahara to a spiritual master of the blade. Harakiri (1962) | Setting: 1630 (Early Edo Period) | The wars have ended, leaving thousands of samurai unemployed and disillusioned by the hypocrisy of the ruling class. Silence (2016) | Setting: 1637 (Shimabara Rebellion) | The violent end of Western influence and the total isolation of the island nation. Blue Eye Samurai (2023) | Setting: c. 1650s | A gritty tale of vengeance taking place during the height of Japan’s "closed door" policy. Lone Wolf and Cub: Sword of Vengeance (1972) | Setting: ~1650s | The dark underbelly of the Shogun's power and the corruption of the secret police. IV. THE GOLDEN AGE & STAGNATION Samurai as bureaucrats, poets, and secret executioners. 47 Ronin / Chushingura (1962) | Setting: 1701–1703 (Genroku Era) | The ultimate test of feudal loyalty in an era where samurai had become peaceful bureaucrats. Zatoichi (2003) | Setting: 1830s–1840s | The blind "anti-samurai" hero protecting the weak from the gambling dens and yakuza of a stagnant era. 13 Assassins (2010) | Setting: 1844 (Late Edo Period) | A final, ritualized suicide mission to stop a sadistic Lord before the Shogunate system collapses. V. THE END OF THE WAY The arrival of the West, the Fall of the Shogun, and the birth of Modern Japan. The Twilight Samurai (2002) | Setting: Early 1860s (Bakumatsu) | The heartbreaking reality of the "working class" samurai—poor, hungry, and facing an obsolete future. Yojimbo (1961) | Setting: 1860 | A nameless ronin navigates a world where traditional honor is being choked out by greed and the arrival of the revolver. Rurouni Kenshin: The Beginning (2021) | Setting: 1864 | The bloody revolution in the streets of Kyoto as the "hitokiri" assassins clash with the Shogunate’s secret police. Lady Snowblood (1973) | Setting: 1874 (Early Meiji) | A stylish revenge masterpiece set during the cold transition to a Westernized legal system. The Last Samurai (2003) | Setting: 1876–1877 (Satsuma Rebellion) | The final, tragic stand of the traditionalist "Old Guard" against modern Gatling guns and progress. Rurouni Kenshin (2012) | Setting: 1878 (Meiji Era) | The aftermath. Carrying a sword is a crime, and survivors must find a new way to live in a world that no longer needs warriors.
